name: clojure-ring-api
title: Clojure Ring API
blurb: Ring JSON service on deps.edn: handler is a plain request-map function, ring.mock drives the routes, Jetty serves them, clojure.test gates it
default_description: A JSON service in Clojure with Ring.

verify.name: http
verify.cmd: PORT=5414 clojure -M -m {{ package_name }}.server >.ring.log 2>&1 & srv=$!; ready=1; for _ in $(seq 1 240); do if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:5414/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=0; break; fi; sleep 0.5; done; if [ $ready -ne 0 ]; then cat .ring.log; kill $srv 2>/dev/null; exit 1; fi; health=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5414/health); stats=$(curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:5414/stats?text=hello%20world%0A'); posted=$(curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{"text":"a b\nc\n"}' http://127.0.0.1:5414/stats); bad=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5414/stats); missing=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5414/nope); kill $srv 2>/dev/null; wait $srv 2>/dev/null || true; cat .ring.log; test "$health" = 200 && printf '%s' "$stats" | grep -q '"lines":1' && printf '%s' "$stats" | grep -q '"bytes":12' && printf '%s' "$posted" | grep -q '"words":3' && test "$bad" = 422 && test "$missing" = 404
